title: Reactive Angular with Signals
subtitle: Model UI state with signal, computed and effect, then go zoneless.

lessons.title: Why signals?
lessons.summary: How fine-grained reactivity replaces zone-based change detection and what that means for performance.

lessons.title: signal, computed and effect
paragraphs: A signal is a value container that notifies consumers when it changes. Read it by calling it, update it with set or update.
computed derives a read-only signal from other signals. It is lazy and memoized: it only recalculates when a dependency changes and someone reads it.
effect runs side effects when the signals it reads change. Keep effects for synchronising with the outside world, such as storage, logging or imperative DOM APIs, not for deriving state.

lessons.title: Going zoneless
paragraphs: Since Angular 21, new applications run without zone.js. Change detection is scheduled by signal writes, template events and the async pipe.
Prefer OnPush components, keep state in signals and avoid mutating objects that templates read directly.

questions.prompt: Which API should you use to derive a value from other signals?
questions.explanation: computed creates a memoized, read-only derived signal.

questions.prompt: What schedules change detection in a zoneless application?
options: Signal writes, template events and the async pipe

title: Cloud Architecture Foundations
subtitle: Design resilient, cost-aware systems on any major cloud.

lessons.title: Well-architected pillars
lessons.summary: Operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimisation and sustainability.

lessons.title: Designing for failure
paragraphs: Assume every dependency will fail. Use timeouts, retries with jitter and circuit breakers at every network boundary.
Spread workloads across availability zones and make deployments immutable so you can roll back quickly.

questions.prompt: Which pattern stops calling a failing dependency for a while?

title: Applied Machine Learning
subtitle: From a clean dataset to a monitored model in production.

lessons.title: Framing the problem
lessons.summary: Turning a business question into a measurable prediction task with a baseline to beat.

lessons.title: Evaluation that matches reality
paragraphs: Split data by time when the model will predict the future; random splits leak information.
Choose metrics that reflect the cost of mistakes. Precision and recall often matter more than accuracy on imbalanced data.

lessons.title: Monitoring models in production
paragraphs: Track input drift, prediction drift and business KPIs. Alert on sustained change, not single spikes.
Keep a human-reviewed feedback loop so labels keep flowing back into retraining.

title: Secure Coding Essentials
subtitle: Prevent the most common web vulnerabilities by design.

lessons.title: Threat modelling in 15 minutes
lessons.summary: Use STRIDE on a data-flow diagram to find the risks that matter before writing code.
